dossiers.title: Homeworld Remastered Collection
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Players command space fleets on a fully three-dimensional battlefield, using altitude, formations, firing arcs, salvage and ship class interactions to plan engagements.
The collection offers campaigns for Homeworld and Homeworld 2, their classic editions and remastered skirmishes; story-driven missions carry forces and resource decisions forward.
Fleet-scale visual effects, upgraded ship models and music make large encounters striking, while the first game's story receives sustained praise.
Veterans repeatedly object that replacing the original Homeworld 1 simulation with modified Homeworld 2 systems alters fighter tactics, refueling, attack behaviour and formations.
Fleet persistence, research, harvesting and capturing enemy ships reward preparation across consecutive missions, but can be affected by how the campaign scales its opposing forces.
Controlling a 3D fleet takes practice, and resource management or adaptive mission forces can make mistakes costly, while the tutorial and readable orders ease initial learning.

Historical player feedback reports collisions, ship movement AI and formation bugs; other reports following 2016 patches describe significant improvements, so these reports do not prove current breakage.
Skirmish and multiplayer extend beyond the story, but some launch-era players reported hanging matches and balance concerns; multiplayer is not a cooperative story campaign.
Launch-era Russian discussion reported missing subtitles during part of the first campaign and a desire for familiar Russian dubbing, without establishing present language coverage.
The campaigns deliver extended tactical space-opera storytelling, although long encounters and the combined engine's different balance can shift their original tempo.

conflicts.statement: Some reviewers regard the remaster as a faithful, accessible revitalization after later patches; others say the changed tactics still make the classic original preferable.

dossiers.title: Citizen Sleeper 2: Starward Vector
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The narrative RPG assigns rolled dice to work, relationships and risky contract actions, while stress, broken dice, food and fuel make choices more consequential than in its predecessor.
Character classes and their Push skills change dice odds, with crew recruitment, equipment, skills and ships enabling more varied contract strategies.
The Sleeper travels between several stations and space habitats, taking timed contracts and meeting separate communities rather than remaining on one fixed station.
Intimate prose, melancholic electronic music, character portraits and themes of freedom, mutual care and survival remain strong attractions.
Some players find stress cascades, failed dice and the early learning curve harsh, particularly for less forgiving classes; others find careful low-risk rolls make contracts easy.
A few players find later economic surpluses and predictable optimal character abilities undermine the early survival tension and choice consequences.
Although space travel broadens locations, some players feel repeated short stops limit attachment to individual settlements and crew arcs or make choices appear illusory.

Russian-language feedback discusses reliance on a fan-made Russian translation because official Russian text was not provided for the reviewed version; the availability and quality of unofficial patches are player reports, not guaranteed current services.
Certain gameplay complaints focus on poor explanation of contract consumption, class balance and stress recovery, in tension with more forgiving lower difficulty modes.

conflicts.statement: Players disagree whether dice damage produces gripping survival decisions or a punishing spiral that can also become trivial after optimization.
Expanded travel and crew storytelling delight some returning players, but others find the sequel's relationships and choices less deeply developed.

dossiers.title: Risk of Rain (2013)
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: A 2D platforming roguelike combines four-character skills, fast combat, randomly ordered areas and increasingly large enemy waves before activating each level's teleporter.
Difficulty steadily intensifies with elapsed time, so looting and exploration compete against keeping pace with enemy scaling, leading to frequent but teachable defeats.
Unlockable survivors, artifacts and new items expand the variety of runs; item stacks interact strongly to transform characters into powerful late-run builds.
Procedural stages and randomized loot enable many attempts, but some players find a limited map pool and the repeated teleporter search or long runs fatiguing.
Four-player cooperative play changes the challenge and supports shared tactics, yet individual item allocation and network synchronization sometimes create friction.
One-shot mistakes and erratic loot distributions sometimes overshadow pure execution skill, especially before characters and items are unlocked.
Retro pixel scenery, alien planetary atmosphere and an energetic soundtrack draw repeated praise in both solo and cooperative play.
The original game's controller and interface design can feel awkward compared with later series releases, and older dated accounts describe occasional co-op sync issues.
A late-2025 Russian review reported trouble returning after focus switched away from the game window; this one account alone cannot establish a persistent widespread technical fault.
Runs can occupy roughly forty to ninety minutes with no mid-run saves; a player deciding how long to loot faces increasing pressure each minute.

conflicts.statement: Some players appreciate the escalating challenge as skill-dependent, while others say particular item drops or multiplayer item allocation dominate success.
